exposure: Mode of first delivery (emergency vs. planned caesarean)
History of failed induction of labor
outcome: Vaginal birth after caesarean section (VBAC) attempt
cohort: 143,970 women in England whose first birth was a live singleton delivered by caesarean section
finding: The study found that 52.2% of women with a prior cesarean section attempted a VBAC, and of those, 63.4% were successful, with success rates varying by maternal age, ethnicity, and history of emergency caesarean section or failed induction of labor.
mod_finding: Younger women and women of white ethnicity had higher success rates of vaginal birth after caesarean section, while Black women had a particularly low success rate. Women who had an emergency caesarean section in their first birth also had a lower VBAC success rate, particularly those with a history of failed induction of labor.
